name: Indiana

code.name: Indiana Code (Title 3, Elections)
code.edition: not read: the Code is served by the Indiana General Assembly's site only as a script application; the rules below rest on the Indiana Election Division's 2026 Election Administrator's Manual (revised April 2026), a state agency guide that cites the Code sections

in-manual-2026.citation: Indiana Election Division, 2026 Indiana Election Administrator's Manual (revised April 2026), pp. 291-296: 'Recount & Contest Actions', 'State Recount Commission', 'Resolving Tie Votes' (citing IC 3-12-6, 3-12-9, 3-12-10, 3-12-11, 3-13-1)
in-manual-2026.note: A state agency's guide, a lower grade than the statute; it states the rule and cites the Code section but the Code's own words were not read.

ties.applies_to: a tie vote at a primary election (any office)
ties.steps: a tie vote at a primary election results in a candidate vacancy; the vacancy is filled through a caucus of eligible precinct committeemen, the party chairman (if the county committee has given the chairman authority), or a caucus of party officers
ties.who: the party (precinct committeemen caucus, party chairman or caucus of party officers)

sources.quote: Whenever a tie vote occurs at a primary election, a “CANDIDATE VACANCY” results. (IC 3-13-1-17) The resulting vacancy is filled through a caucus of eligible precinct committeemen, the party chairman (if the chairman has received authority from the county committee to fill candidate vacancies), or a caucus of party officers. (IC 3-13-1-6)

ties.note: From the Election Division's manual, citing IC 3-13-1-17 and 3-13-1-6; the Code's words were not read.

ties.applies_to: a general election tie for a federal office, a state office other than governor and lieutenant governor, or a legislative office
ties.steps: a special election is held to break the tie

sources.quote: In a general election, a tie vote occurring in a federal, state (other than governor and lieutenant governor), or legislative office requires a special election to break the tie. (IC 3-12-9-1)

ties.note: From the manual, citing IC 3-12-9-1. 'Legislative office' is read to cover the General Assembly [inferred]; whether a recount comes before the special election is not stated.

ties.applies_to: a tie vote for the office of governor or lieutenant governor
ties.steps: the tie is resolved at a joint session of the State Senate and House of Representatives
ties.who: the General Assembly in joint session

sources.quote: A tie vote for the office of governor and [...] lieutenant governor is resolved at a joint session of the State Senate and House of Representatives. (IC 3-12-9-2)

ties.note: From the manual, citing IC 3-12-9-2; [...] marks a page break in the manual (page 295 to 296).

ties.applies_to: a tie vote at an election for a local office or a school board office
ties.steps: the circuit court clerk sends written notice of the tie to the fiscal body of the political subdivision; the fiscal body resolves the tie by electing a person to fill the office, not later than December 31 following the election
ties.who: the fiscal body of the political subdivision (county council, city-county council, common council, town council, township board and so on); the executive of the subdivision may cast the deciding vote in a fiscal body tie; if the tie is among school board members, the circuit court judge selects one candidate certified as elected (IC 20-23-4-30)

sources.quote: Whenever a circuit court clerk receives certification that a tie vote at an election for a local office or school board office has occurred, the clerk shall immediately send written notice of the tie vote to the fiscal body of the affected political subdivision. (IC 3-12-9-3)
A fiscal body notified by the circuit court clerk of a tie vote resolves the tie by electing a person to fill the office not later than December 31 following the election at which the vote occurred.

ties.note: From the manual, citing IC 3-12-9-3 to 3-12-9-5. The 'legislature' resolution is used for a local legislative or fiscal body deciding for itself. State general law only; charters were not read.
The manual's section on resolving tie votes names no presidential electors and no public question. The Code itself was not read, so no absence is claimed.

threshold.conditions: verified petition in the circuit or superior court of the county not later than noon, 14 days after the election (the candidate's county chairman, 17 days; a cross-petition, 21 days); the petitioner states the precincts to be recounted and posts a bond or cash deposit of at least $100, raised by $10 or $100 for every precinct over ten, depending on whether the candidate lost by more or less than 1%
threshold.in_words: a candidate for a judicial, local or school board office may petition for a recount of chosen precincts whatever the margin; there is no automatic recount

who_may_request: a candidate seeking nomination or election to a judicial, local or school board office, or for the party office of precinct committeeman or state convention delegate
the candidate's political county chairman, if the candidate does not file
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, by bond or cash deposit, refunded in full if the recount petition is successful (partial refunds may follow); costs left unpaid after the deposit are paid from the county general fund

sources.quote: There are no automatic recount or contest actions in Indiana.

A candidate seeking nomination or election to a judicial, local or school board office, or a candidate for election to the party office of precinct committeeman or state convention delegate may request that the votes cast for that office be recounted. (IC 3-12-6-1)

file a bond or cash deposit of at least $100 with the court for payment of costs of the recount. For every precinct over ten to be recounted, the bond or cash amount should be increased by $10 per precinct or $100 per precinct, depending upon whether the candidate lost by more or less than 1%.
If the recount petition is successful, the petitioner’s deposit or bond is refunded in full.

recounts.note: From the manual, citing IC 3-12-6; the Code's words were not read. 'No margin required' is the reader's reading of the manual's silence on any margin condition [inferred]. The manual's mention of 'a voter entitled to ask for a recount of the public question' (elsewhere in the manual, in its section on certifying results) suggests a recount of a local public question exists; its terms were not stated and are not recorded.

threshold.conditions: the verified petition is filed with the Indiana Election Division, not earlier than 10 days after the election; the State Recount Commission conducts the recount; if the petitioner loses by more than 10% of the total votes cast, the petitioner is responsible for the costs of the recount otherwise charged to another candidate or cross-petitioner
threshold.in_words: a candidate may petition the State Recount Commission for a recount of a federal, statewide or state legislative office whatever the margin; there is no automatic recount

who_may_request: a candidate (petition to the State Recount Commission through the Indiana Election Division)
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, as for a local recount, and responsible for the commission's costs if the petitioner loses by more than 10% of the total votes cast

sources.quote: Recount requests for federal, statewide, or state legislative offices are handled by the State Recount Commission; please see the “State Recount Commission” section below for those details. (IC 3-12-11-1)

The state recount commission conducts recounts and hears contests for Presidential primaries and nominations for a federal, statewide, or state legislative office, and conducts recounts of election for federal, statewide, or state legislative offices.

(2) If a candidate or other petitioner who requested a recount loses by more than 10% of the total votes cast, the petitioner is responsible for the costs of the recount otherwise charged to another candidate or cross-petitioner;

recounts.note: From the manual, citing IC 3-12-10 and 3-12-11; the Code's words were not read. 'No margin required' is the reader's reading of the manual's silence on any margin condition [inferred]. The manual says the commission also hears contests, which are litigation and are not recorded.

notes: Indiana rests on the Election Division's 2026 Election Administrator's Manual, a state agency guide (the earlier reader used the same manual's pages 291-295); every rule is marked 'stated' for that reason. The Code's own words should be read before the rules are shown as law.

Surprising rules: there is no automatic recount at any margin; a primary tie is a candidate vacancy filled by party caucus; a general election tie for an office other than governor and lieutenant governor is a special election; a tie for governor or lieutenant governor goes to the General Assembly in joint session; a local tie is settled by the local fiscal body electing a person.
